left.note: third look: EDGE, placed by the geometry of the frame. No visible line: the foliage background reads exactly at base in level, colour and noise, and its faint texture is no more repeatable across the three scans (s_09, b0922b_10, b0921a_17) in cols 7-23 than in 0-6. Only the sky highlights are film. Two measurements that do not use this side at all settled it. (1) FRAME WIDTH. This picture's RIGHT edge is a real, straight cut in b0922b_09's left sliver: many specks end on one vertical line at ~41.0, then certain base (42-61), then the next picture at 62.1. Registered into s_09 (k=400.6) that edge is at ~441.6. Six clean frames of this walk, each with its left edge in s_n and its right edge from the b-walk sliver registered into s_n, give a gate width W = 435.0-436.2 (mean 435.5), so the left edge is at ~6.1 +-0.7. For picture_to_border, W would have to be >=441.6, six columns wider than every other frame. (2) GAP. The neighbour's right edge in b0922b_10 is at 42.4, and five gaps on this roll measure 18.5-21.8, which puts the picture start at 5.9-9.2 here. (3) HIGHLIGHTS: the row-98 sky patch is already at ~75% of full density at col 7, and col 6 is at base in every row, so hi is 7.3. The leaves 'tapering' at cols 7-8 are compatible with a cut. L1's cols 0-6 are right, but the gate may be up to a column left of where the first speck sits. The row-222 speck at col 7 is a single one-channel pixel, like the noise hits in cols 0-5, so I don't count it.
